questions.q: Name the three states of water.
How does ice change to water and water to vapour?
questions.a: Heating melts ice to water; more heating boils water into vapour.

questions.q: How does water vapour turn back to liquid?
questions.a: On cooling, vapour condenses into water drops (as on a cold lid).
A liquid turning into vapour - wet clothes dry as water evaporates.
Vapour cooling back into liquid - drops form on a mirror over hot water.

questions.q: How do evaporation and condensation work together at home?
questions.a: Boiling water makes vapour; a cold plate held over it shows drops - a mini water cycle.

questions.q: Why does the hand feel cool after sprinkling water?
questions.a: Evaporating water takes heat from the skin, cooling it.

questions.q: Why do we wear cotton in summer?
questions.a: Cotton absorbs sweat, and its evaporation cools the body.

questions.q: Give one more example of cooling by evaporation.
questions.a: Earthen pots (matkas) cool water as it seeps out and evaporates.

questions.q: Name the main steps of the water cycle.
questions.a: Evaporation of water, condensation into clouds, rainfall, and flow of water back to seas.
The sun - its heat evaporates water and drives winds that move clouds.

questions.q: Why is the water cycle important for us?
questions.a: It renews fresh water on land as rain, feeding rivers, wells and crops.
